answer:
**With no labels and a one-day deadline, the first deliverable is a narrow, testable behavior.** Choose a task with clear inputs, outputs, and an abstention path. A small human-reviewed evaluation set is needed even if the first implementation uses prompting or rules rather than supervised training. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10160)

For ticket categorization, a keyword baseline may handle obvious cases while a pretrained model handles varied phrasing. Compare them on the same examples, including ambiguous and unsupported requests. Record correctness, coverage, latency, and the cost of mistakes.

**Do not confuse generating labels with validating them.** Synthetic examples can help later training or distillation, but a model labeling its own outputs can reproduce its blind spots. Verify a representative subset independently and preserve real edge cases.

Ship a reversible workflow with human review where confidence is insufficient, collect corrections, and expand only after evidence supports it. Transfer learning is valuable because it reuses learned representations; it does not remove the need to evaluate the actual task. The deadline should narrow scope, not redefine unmeasured quality as success.

**Technical details and references.**

For tomorrow, define a narrow supported task, collect a small human-reviewed evaluation set, and ship a reversible baseline with abstention. Zero-shot prompting is fast for language tasks but needs evidence and output checks. Heuristics/weak supervision encode domain knowledge and are easy to inspect. Transfer learning reuses a pretrained representation with limited adaptation. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10160)

Synthetic examples plus distillation can reduce serving cost later, but generated labels need independent verification and diversity; zero real labels means quality is not established. Compare correctness, coverage, latency, and cost on the same examples. Start with human review for uncertain cases and collect corrections for training. A launch deadline does not substitute for an evaluation baseline.
